title: CompletionVerdict
description: Output of the rebar.llm completion-verification operation (`rebar verify-completion <id>`): a PASS/FAIL verdict that a ticket's completion criteria (acceptance/success/close/completion criteria, definitions of done; for bugs, resolution) are demonstrably met by the implementation. SHAPE-ONLY: the FAIL⇔findings invariant and verdict normalization are enforced by the operation's `reconcile_verdict` (code), not the schema, because the runner validates this schema BEFORE the operation can repair a sloppy model turn. `verdict` is `string` (not a strict enum) so the operation can normalize casing. Each FAIL finding reuses the canonical `finding` shape with an added `criterion` (the specific requirement that failed). The MCP `verify_completion` tool returns this shape as a plain dict but advertises no outputSchema (live LLM call — a documented NO_SCHEMA_EXEMPT).

verdict.description: PASS or FAIL (normalized by the operation; not a strict enum so model casing can be repaired).

verdict_obtainable.description: OPTIONAL framework-set marker (never model-supplied). Present and `false` ONLY when the verifier returned a non-PASS result naming no criterion and none could be recovered from `criteria` — i.e. no verdict was obtainable at all. That is a VERIFIER FAULT, not a judgement that a criterion is unmet, and callers map it to a retryable exit (11) with a distinct message rather than reporting fabricated unmet criteria. It rides ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary rather than adding a third verdict token, so `verdict` stays `FAIL` and every existing consumer still blocks fail-closed. Absent on every other verdict.

evidence_sufficient.description: OPTIONAL framework-derived marker (never trusted from model output; `reconcile_verdict` re-derives it from the per-criterion markers). Present and `false` ONLY on a FAIL whose every unmet criterion carries the per-criterion `evidence_sufficient: false` marker — i.e. the bounded evidence search was exhausted without finding evidence and NOTHING was positively refuted. Insufficiency, not refutation: like `verdict_obtainable` it rides ALONGSIDE the PASS/FAIL vocabulary, so `verdict` stays `FAIL`, every fail-closed consumer still blocks, and only message rendering and the recorded evidence class change. Absent on every other verdict.

findings.description: One finding per FAILING criterion (empty on PASS). Reuses the canonical `finding` shape; the failing requirement rides on `finding.criterion` (an additional property). A finding may also carry an optional `remediation` string — a per-finding next move (for an operator-attested criterion judged NOT MET: record proof as a ticket comment/artifact naming the reference, observed outcome, and when) — distinct from the top-level generic `remediation`.

criteria.description: OPTIONAL positive per-criterion evaluation records — the lossless PASS capture that rides alongside the failures-only `findings`. One record per evaluated criterion (met or not). Empty/absent on the legacy path.

criterion.description: The evaluated criterion (verbatim or clearly identifying).

met.description: Whether this criterion is demonstrably met.

evidence_sufficient.description: OPTIONAL framework-set marker (never model-supplied; the banking/merge seams own it). Present and `false` ONLY when this record is the bounded fallback's insufficiency record: the finite evidence search was exhausted without demonstrating the criterion, so `met: false` here is an evidence GAP, not a positive refutation. Absent on every other record.

citation.description: Evidence for the evaluation (nullable): file+line / url / freeform source.

summary.description: Optional verifier summary; carries the no-explicit-criteria PASS rationale when applicable.

remediation.description: Guidance carried on a FAIL verdict (set by the operation's `reconcile_verdict`): how to satisfy the unmet criteria, including documenting evidence that meets a requirement as a comment on the ticket — the verifier reads a ticket's comments, so recorded evidence is taken into account on the next verification. Absent on PASS (nothing to remediate).

certifiable.description: Whether the close may be CERTIFIED (signed). False iff a direct child is closed-but-uncertified (force-closed) — the parent may close but not certify, because certification propagates: an unattested descendant leaves the subtree unattested. Absent/true on the common path. Does not affect the PASS/FAIL verdict (the parent's own criteria stand); the close gate reads it to close without signing.

model.description: Model id used (null for non-LLM/fake runners).

trace_id.description: Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled; null otherwise.

coverage.description: Additive observability about how this run was produced. Present ONLY when there is something to report, so a clean run omits it entirely and its verdict stays byte-identical - which matters here because this verdict is SIGNED. Never changes the verdict, exit code, signature, or provenance stamp. The key mirrors review-plan and review-code so one JSON path reaches the tally on every gate.

llm_step_failures.description: LLM step calls that FAILED but did not fail this run - the non-fatal degradation that used to be visible only in the logs (e.g. every overlap-judge batch dying, so an empty overlap[] was indistinguishable from 'nothing overlapped'). Present ONLY when at least one call failed, so a clean run's coverage is byte-identical; purely additive - it never changes the verdict, exit code, signature, or provenance stamp. Reaching the verdict at all means the run survived these, which is what makes them non-fatal.

total.description: Number of failed LLM step calls in this run.

by_step.description: Failure count per step, keyed by the runner's call label VERBATIM so a key matches the 'llm call [<label>] ... FAILED' log line. The label is the joined reviewer list when a call has one (e.g. 'overlap-judge') and otherwise falls back to the target ticket id, or the literal '?' when even that is absent - so calls carrying no reviewer list group under that fallback key rather than under a step name.
